inspectionNotes: Original supplied image was opened before external research. Temporary crop enlarged existing pixels for inspection only; it adds no detail or new map content and is not proposed for publication. Original Site asset unchanged.

LOC's four transcriptions are Wichquawank, Techkonis, Mareckweich and Keskachauc. The Center for Brooklyn History lists similarly spelled communities, but the strongest exact-name bridge is Techkonis. Other spellings are not silently equated or georeferenced.

The finding aid is not used merely as a catalogue title or subject tag: its actual substantive historical note explicitly identifies documented Munsee communities. That is the inspected evidence. It cites Robert S. Grumet, American Indians, in The Encyclopedia of New York City (1995), pages 25–28; those underlying pages and WPA typescripts were not read.

Munsee-Delaware Nation's opening self-description is used narrowly. The page's compressed subgroup taxonomy and linguistic wording are not adopted as a general classification. Its site does not claim a Techkonis-specific descent link, and none is invented.

The Delaware Tribe of Indians' existing Lenape History page was actually opened; its introductory Delaware Valley framing does not identify Techkonis and is not treated as village corroboration. Linked publications were not read for this task.

A relevant NYC-hosted archaeological assessment, https://s-media.nyc.gov/agencies/lpc/arch_reports/1856.pdf, surfaced as a lead but actual web fetch rejected its size. Search excerpts are not adopted as inspected evidence. No report, manuscript or modern archaeological site location is relied on.

Wikipedia, mirrors, unsourced derivatives and commercial results are excluded. No original creation narrative, restricted knowledge, private record, human remains or precise archaeological location is accessed or reproduced.

These are educational historical-map relationships only. No source-count increase or content-review upgrade to the three canonical profiles, new access point, main-data edit or publication is performed.
